props.title: Old Joy

sections.content: Old Joy (2006) represents a pivotal moment in American independent cinema's "mumblecore" movement, though it transcends that label. Director Kelly Reichardt crafts a deceptively simple tale of two old friends reuniting for a weekend camping trip in Oregon's Cascade Mountains. Like Reichardt's later Wendy and Lucy (2008) and First Cow (2019), it explores male friendship and American alienation through careful observation and minimal dialogue. The film shares DNA with European slow cinema like The Turin Horse (2011), but remains distinctly Pacific Northwestern in its misty landscapes and ecological undertones.

sections.content: The film's influence rippled through 2000s independent cinema, inspiring a wave of contemplative character studies like Into the Wild (2007) and All the Real Girls (2003). Will Oldham's performance as Kurt exemplifies the era's blurring of music and film scenes, similar to Justin Vernon in Shut Up and Play the Hits (2012). Reichardt's minimalist approach influenced later directors like Jim Jarmusch's Paterson (2016) and Sean Baker's The Florida Project (2017). SUBHEAD: The New American Landscape Film

Reichardt pioneered a distinctly American approach to landscape cinema, different from European predecessors. While Paris, Texas (1984) used vast spaces to represent emotional isolation, Old Joy makes Oregon's forests intimate and claustrophobic. This technique influenced later films like Leave No Trace (2018) and Captain Fantastic (2016), where nature becomes both refuge and trap. The film's environmental consciousness predates the eco-anxiety of First Reformed (2017) and Dark Waters (2019).
